principles.principle: The conclusion opens by making the paper itself (or 'we') the grammatical subject and restating what the study set out to do or show, before any specific result is revisited.
principles.why: Re-stating the goal up front re-orients a reader who arrives at the end, and frames everything that follows as the payoff to a declared mission rather than a loose pile of findings.

evidence.quote: The primary objective of this paper is to document systematic behavioral differences in corporate decision-making across managers.
This paper shows that CEOs persistently differ in the clarity of their communication.
In sum, this paper offers an initial attempt to bring to the fore the problem of adverse selection in corporate strategy

principles.principle: Key findings are introduced by a leading phrase that ties the result to an ex ante prediction or to prior work — 'Consistent with ...,' 'in line with prior evidence ...' — placed before the finding itself.
principles.why: Putting the interpretive frame first tells the reader how to read a result the moment it arrives, signalling that the evidence confirms a stated expectation and binding the recap back to the paper's theory.

evidence.quote: Consistent with the free cash f low hypothesis, these acquisitions by cash-rich firms are value decreasing
Consistent with our estimates measuring the underlying latent components of linguistic complexity, we find a predicted negative (positive) relation
which is in line with prior evidence that firms that manipulate earnings to beat expectations are still able to benefit from higher stock returns, but also larger long-term losses.

principles.principle: The summary is narrated through active first-person agents and the personified paper: research verbs take 'we'/'I' or 'this paper/our paper' as their grammatical subject, so each claim is attached to an actor who performed it rather than floated as an abstract finding.
principles.why: Active, attributed sentences read faster and more confidently than passive abstraction; the reader always knows who did what, and personifying the artifact lets a single subject carry the contribution cleanly while keeping the prose direct and accountable.

evidence.quote: We develop an empirical framework to analyze the importance of a manager dimension in the observed unexplained variation in several corporate practices.
To test whether cash stockpiles are invested poorly, I study the acquisition behavior of cash-rich firms. I find that cash-rich firms are more likely to make acquisitions.
This paper shows that CEOs persistently differ in the clarity of their communication.
This paper contributes to prior literature by investigating whether stock-for-stock M&As induce managers to strategically manipulate the content of corporate disclosures

principles.device: Connective signposting of an ordered recap
principles.principle: Findings are stitched into a staged sequence by placing additive or ordinal discourse markers — First, Second, Moreover, Further, Finally — at the head of successive sentences.
principles.why: The connectives tell the reader exactly where each claim sits in the argument and signal how many points remain, giving a dense results recap an easy-to-follow spine.

evidence.quote: First, by examining all words that occur in at least 5% of the SEC's 10-K universe, we create a list of words that we believe typically have a negative meaning in financial reports.
Moreover, managers with higher performance fixed effects receive higher levels of compensation and are more likely to be found in firms where ownership is more concentrated.
Further, there is some evidence that cash-rich firms with greater likelihood of agency problems, as evidenced by low managerial stock ownership, account for the acquisition activity.

principles.principle: Claims are routinely bounded and qualified, characteristically through a 'While X ..., Y' concessive that admits a limitation and immediately pivots to the contribution that survives it, reinforced by hedging verbs ('suggest', 'appears', 'some evidence', 'caveat').
principles.why: Naming the obvious objection first signals scientific caution and disarms a skeptical reader; the concessive shape converts an admitted weakness into a pivot that protects the contribution rather than undercutting it.

evidence.quote: While the framework we follow does not allow us to estimate the causal effect of managers on firm policies or performance, it provides a simple and intuitive approach to deal with many of the first-order selection problems that such a study might face.
While the evidence we provide speaks somewhat to the latter argument, we ultimately leave this interesting question for future research.
One important caveat to our decomposition approach is that we cannot speak to the generalizability of the approach outside of the conference call setting

Finally, the market appears to anticipate this, but for a variety of reasons not yet fully understood, external control mechanisms do not act to correct the failures of internal mechanisms in cash-rich firms.

principles.principle: The section ends by turning away from what was done toward what is next and what it means: open future-research questions and directives, and prescriptions that cash the findings out for practitioners ('we recommend', 'should exercise caution', 'leave ... for future research', 'we hope ... encourages future research').
principles.why: Closing on an agenda and on stakes gives the summary momentum and relevance instead of a flat recap, framing the paper as a foundation others will build on and giving the reader a reason to care beyond the results themselves.

evidence.quote: Regardless, our findings suggest that regulators and researchers should exercise caution when assuming that complex language is necessarily less informative than simple language.
Given our results, we recommend the use of term weighting when creating word counts.
we ultimately leave this interesting question for future research.
we hope that our study encourages future research that better accounts for the implications of M&A for other factor markets.

principles.principle: Abstract constructs are made tangible with concrete exemplars (named figures, real listed words), and the prose lands short, aphoristic sentences that compress the message into a memorable phrase.
principles.why: Concreteness makes an intangible measure vivid and easy to grasp, while a crisp, quotable closing line gives the summary a resonant landing that an abstract restatement cannot achieve.

evidence.quote: Some, like former Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke, are clear talkers and thus quite informative. Others, like Alan Greenspan, are fuzzy talkers; their style clouds their message.
Common words like depreciation, liability, foreign, and board are not tonal when occurring in a 10-K.
In short, the results of our study suggest that silence speaks.
All textual analysis ultimately stands or falls by the categorization procedures.

side_notes: Synthesis collapses 16 principles to 7 distinct devices: (1) agentive voice [a3-p1], (2) mission-recap opener [a1-p1], (3) signposted/ordinal sequencing [a1-p3], (4) concede-and-qualify/hedging [a3-p3], (5) forward-looking close [a3-p4], (6) aphoristic clinching line + concrete anchors [a3-p5], (7) fronted theory-anchored framing [a1-p6]. Mission-recap (a1-p1) and agentive voice (a3-p1) are kept separate on purpose: one is a structural opening move, the other a pervasive sentence-construction choice; a2-p1 and a3-p2 each bundled the recap with another device, but a1-p1 is its sole clean carrier so nothing is lost by merging those bundles elsewhere.

Canonical-selection note: for the concede group (G3), forward-close group (G4), and aphoristic/concrete group (G5) the agent-3 versions were chosen because they carry the most published-journal evidence (QJE/JF/JAR) and, for a3-p5, are the superset (they also capture the concrete-exemplar device that no other principle names). For the voice group, a3-p1 was preferred over a1-p2 despite a1-p2's purer evidence, because a1-p2 captures only first-person 'we find' and omits the heavily-evidenced paper-as-actor personification ('This paper shows/contributes').

COVERAGE GAP: all three agents operated at the sentence and discourse-move level (opener, voice, connectives, concessives, closer, takeaway). None examined paragraph-level / macro-structure: how the conclusion is chunked into paragraphs, topic-sentence patterns, or the proportion of recap versus implications. A human should decide whether this level needs its own principles.

COVERAGE GAP: lexical register and diction (formality, plain-versus-latinate word choice, technical-jargon density) is unexamined except the narrow 'concrete exemplars' observation folded into a3-p5. No principle treats word choice itself as a style device.

COVERAGE GAP / TENSION: the active-voice principles (a3-p1 and merged a1-p2, a2-p1) never examined the impersonal and passive constructions that coexist in the very same conclusions and evidence -- 'there is some evidence that...', 'managers... are more likely to be found...', 'the market appears to anticipate...'. The claimed uniform active voice may be overstated; tense usage (present 'we find' vs past) is likewise unexamined.

COVERAGE GAP: sentence-level mechanics beyond connectives and aphoristic brevity -- sentence-length variation, parallel structure, and punctuation devices visible in the evidence (em-dashes, semicolons such as 'fuzzy talkers; their style clouds their message') -- were left unexamined by all three agents.
